item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is the preferable patch because its retry fix is narrowly targeted at the reported os.Open case and avoids globally buffering arbitrary reader bodies. Both candidates share a significant contract violation: Upload duplicates Add instead of routing through it.","reasons":["B uses io.ReadSeeker to replay file bodies from their original offset, directly addressing Files.Add with os.Open while preserving streaming for non-seekable readers.","A changes RawClient.Do to eagerly read every unrecognized io.Reader unless WithNoRetry is set, creating broad memory and latency changes outside typical file uploads.","B's Upload retry test verifies the multipart file content on every attempt; A's Upload retry test only verifies that two bodies were received, though its separate raw/Add tests provide supporting coverage.","A has better explicit coverage of source-reader failures and FilesOption request headers; B implements error propagation but omits the contract-requested source-reader failure test."],"risks_a":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly and duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data behavior instead of reusing Add.","Global eager buffering can consume unbounded memory, block on streaming readers, and change when reader errors occur.","Buffering replaces io.ReadCloser bodies without closing the original source, changing ownership behavior implicitly."],"risks_b":["Upload also bypasses Add, leaving duplicated behavior that can drift from the required lower-level path.","The new seekable wrapper changes body-closing ownership and shares one mutable ReadSeeker across GetBody instances, which deserves careful review.","No Upload source-reader failure test is included despite the frozen testing contract."]}
